newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Duisenberg warns of costs of EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg warns of costs of EMU delay.

text.p: Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg said on Saturday that a delay to the start of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) was unfeasible because of the huge investments already made in the process.

Duisenberg, who takes over in July as chief of the European Monetary Institute (EMI), said in an interview with Dutch newspaper Het Parool that governments could be even exposed to damages claims if the project was held back.

Banks and capital markets were geared toward the genesis of the single currency on January 1, 1999 -- when central bank operations and sovereign debt issuance will be in euros -- and had laid out large sums to prepare themselves for it, he said.
"Everyone has made massive investments to make that possible...an operation you must not underestimate," he said.

"There are even jurists who come to me and say: 'consider that governments could be held liable for damages suffered if the EMU is postponed.' They took the responsibility for EMU by signing the Maastricht treaty."
Duisenberg said the treaty's convergence criteria should be strictly applied in determining the countries initially admitted to the single currency.
"Countries that...can not take part, I say, must not take part. They should themselves not even want to," he said. "We must do all we can so that they can take part one, two or three years later."
Sustainable fiscal discipline was also vital for the infant euro, he emphasized.
"Everyone always forgets that aside from the accounting criteria, this will also be taken into consideration in the judgement of the economic position of a country."
Duisenberg is widely tipped to be the first head of the supra-national European Central Bank which will take over from the EMI in Frankfurt.
He told Het Parool he had found an apartment in the city on which he had a nine-year lease.
"One year EMI. And the term of office for central bank presidents is eight years. One plus eight is nine."
